scope: Read-only local fixed-tokenizer audit; no model inference, no browser, no threshold/default change
method: Canonical token counts call the locked AutoTokenizer.encode with add_special_tokens:false.

MinimumRegularByteTokens is a dynamic-programming lower bound over the same regular BPE vocabulary decoded by the actual ByteLevelDecoder mapping. It allows non-canonical segmentations and includes globally suppressed lexical tokens, so it is a conservative lower bound for exact bytes.

max_new_tokens is the current production helper result for the correct detected language and original decoded clip duration. Initial decoder prompt is excluded by Transformers.js; timestamps/EOS consume additional new tokens.

Only clips fitting the 10s Tiny / 14s Base production window can attribute whole-reference budget shortage to a single production window. Longer clips require aligned per-window text; full-reference comparison does not prove per-window truncation.

Scoring-normalized variants use existing CER/WER normalization. Their token counts do not prove all score-equivalent strings impossible: punctuation, spaces, script forms, casing and number rendering can change tokenization. Raw exact minimum exceeding budget proves only the exact reference bytes cannot fit, not that every equally scoreable rendering cannot fit.
